title: Praise to Thee, Thou Great Creator
description: Praise to Thee, Thou Great Creator in Tonic Solfa to OMNI DIE, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Fawcett wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 165 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “God of our Salvation”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Eights and Sevens (8.7.8.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to OMNI DIE; any other Eights and Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Praise to thee, thou great Cre-a-tor; Praise be thine from ev-ery tongue; Join, my soul, with ev-ery crea-ture, Join the u-ni-ver-sal song.

lines: Praise to thee, thou great Creator;
Praise be thine from every tongue;
Join, my soul, with every creature,
Hail the God of our salvation;
Praise him for his love divine.
For the hope of future joy,
Sound his praise through earth and heaven,
'Till in heaven our song we raise;
Lost in wonder, love, and praise.

licence: Public domain: John Fawcett died in 1817.
credits: Words by John Fawcett (1740–1817), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to OMNI DIE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
